newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Mixed share moves leave Hungary's BUX almost flat.
newsitem.headline: Mixed share moves leave Hungary's BUX almost flat.

text.p: Hungarian shares performed mixed on Wednesday and the slight rise of the BUX index was not yet indicative of any trend for the near future, dealers said.
"Small increases could happen in the next days but overall, I do not expect a significant rise," said Zoltan Gratzer of Procent Hungaria.
The BUX index opened at 5,320.09 points and after a peak of 5,412.77 points, closed at 5,353.49, up 34.29 or 0.64 percent.
The Budapest bourse started a continuous BUX calculation test on April 1 and the data will probably be available real-time within two weeks.
Some leading shares, suck as OTP Bank and chemicals TVK moved in line with the BUX, chopping off after early gains.
"OTP is one of the shares which move as the market as a whole does," Gratzer said.
OTP shares peaked 4,045 forints and despite retreating later, still put on 125 forints to close at 3,875.
"This is a fair level for the moment, but OTP has the potential to reach 5,000 forints," Gratzer said.
Other papers in the financial sector closed also higher, with Inter-Europa Bank rising 800 forints to end at 48,500, and Quaestor Securities gaining 70 to finish at 2,850.
TVK, the day's most actively traded stock with more than 373,000 shares changing hands, closed at 2,300 forints, up 30.
Elsewhere on the market, hotelier Danubius gained four percent or 205 forints to end at 5,300.
